### Observed differences

- The four-activity block A36/A37/A42/A43 ran in essentially every trace before, but in the later window appears in only about 50 in 100 traces — and the four always appear together or not at all (co-occurrence about 51 in 100, neither about 50 in 100). When the block runs, it sits later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.40 before vs about 0.58 after). [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, REL038]
- A27 shows the same drop, from all traces to about 50 in 100, and in the later window it almost never co-occurs with the block (about 0.5 in 100), so A27 and the block now appear in disjoint sets of traces. [OCC002, POS004, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- A25 now passes almost directly to A28: about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A28, versus about 4 in 100 before (previously about 98 in 100 went to the block), and the A25→A28 gap is 1 step in about 97 in 100 later cases versus 5 steps before. [DIR003, LAG002]
- The old hand-off from the block into A28 disappeared (ordered pairs such as A36→A28 within five steps: about 200 before-traces vs about 1 after), and the block now exits to A31 in about 22–28 in 100 of its transitions, with A31 following within five steps in about 100 later traces versus about 1 before. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG016]
- A26 now routes to A27 in about 49 in 100 cases (before about 98 in 100) and to the block in most of the remainder; its order relative to the block flipped, running before it in about 50 in 100 later traces where it previously followed it in about 98 in 100. [DIR004, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- A06 became rarer (about 32 in 100 traces before vs about 10 in 100 after) and appears earlier and more variably; its exits spread across many targets, with the share going to A52 falling from about 88 in 100 to about 29 in 100. [OCC001, POS001, DIR002]
- A25, A26, A28 and A31 still occur in every trace in both windows; only their positions and relations shifted (e.g., A28's mean relative position about 0.47 → about 0.39). [POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that routing around the A25/A26 segment was restructured: in the later window, about half of the executions skip the A36/A37/A42/A43 block entirely and continue A26 → A27, while the other half skip A27 and run the block after A28 and A26, exiting to A31 instead of back into A28; A25 connects directly to A28 in both patterns. This is shown directly and consistently: participation halves for A27 and the block, the routing shares of A25, A26 and the block move exactly as this rerouting predicts, co-occurrence and order relations flip coherently across dozens of activity pairs, and the affected adjacencies appear or disappear where the rerouting implies. With 96 qualifying evidence items against about 1 expected if nothing had changed, chance alone cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR008, REL018, REL024, REL030, REL034, LAG002, LAG011, LAG013, LAG016]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of pre-existing trace variants rather than a modified structure — the "block-skipping" behaviour could have existed before at very low frequency and simply be absent from the earlier 200-trace sample, although a move from 100 in 100 to about 50 in 100 participation is difficult to attribute to sampling variation alone. Some lag findings also rest on very few later observations (as few as 1–3 traces), and A06's exit-profile change rests on only 17 later transitions, so those details are weaker than the core rerouting pattern. [LAG003, LAG005, LAG011, OCC001, DIR002]

Hmm wait, but in variant 1, does A31 come after A27? REL023: A27 before A31 when both (A_before_B 0.5). And A31 in all traces. So variant 1: ... A27 → ... → A31.

This is getting deep. For the answer, I don't need the full reconstructed model — I need to describe the main behavioural differences and judge support for a structural hypothesis.

Key behavioural differences (later window):
1. A36, A37, A42, A43: participation dropped from ~100% to ~50% of traces; they always occur together (co-occurrence 0.505, neither 0.495) — the whole block is skipped in about half the traces. Their positions moved later (mean ~0.40 → ~0.58 of trace length).

6. A06: participation dropped from ~32% to ~10%; its main exit A52 share fell from ~88% to ~29% (small after-support: 17 transitions).
7. A31: new successor role — the A36-group now exits to A31 (~18–28% each), and A31 follows the group within 5 steps in ~100 traces (vs ~1 before).

Count check: 96 items vs 1.01 expected — many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it. Good.

Now the judgement: The evidence directly supports a structural change: a routing/skip change around the A25/A26 block. The hypothesis: after the change, roughly half of the executions skip the {A36, A37, A42, A43} sub-block (and A27), with A25 proceeding directly to A28 and A26 to A27; in the remaining executions the sub-block is rerouted to run after A28/A26 and now leads to A31, with A27 skipped. This is supported by direct participation, routing (DIR), relational (REL), and lag (LAG) evidence that consistently agree.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The instructions: Supported = "the evidence supports a specific hypothesis directly and consistently." We have:
- Direct participation changes (OCC002–006) showing the block and A27 halved.
- Direct routing changes (DIR003, DIR004, DIR005–008) showing A25 → A28 and A26 → A27/group, group → A31.
- Direct relational evidence (REL012–051) showing co-occurrence/order changes consistent with a skip variant.
- Direct lag evidence (LAG002, LAG003–006, LAG007–016) showing new and disappeared adjacencies.

The consistency across independent indicator types (occurrence, direction, relation, lag, position) on a coherent story is strong. Competing explanations: sampling differences in variant frequencies — the two windows are finite samples of 200 traces each; if the process always had two variants (one with the block, one without) with a 50/50... no wait, before the block appeared in 100% of traces. A shift from 100% to 50% participation cannot plausibly be sampling noise with 200 traces per window (empirical strength 0.995 for each item, and the joint pattern is coherent). Could it be a shift in the mix of two pre-existing variants? Before, all 200 traces had the block; after, ~101 do. If the process had two variants and the window before happened to draw only variant-A traces... possible in principle but with 200 traces all showing the block, the before-window variant mix would have to be extremely skewed. The evidence can't fully rule out a change in the variant mix rather than a structural modification — actually, a change in variant mix IS a behavioural change; the hypothesis is about structure. The instructions say to mention sampling differences in variant frequencies as a competing explanation.
